brief: The S&P 500 trades near record highs, but only about a quarter of its stocks sit above their 50-day averages. Earnings estimates show the same split: the index's Q3 estimate rose 1.2% from 30 June to 31 August, but estimates fell in seven of eleven sectors, and FactSet's pre-September revisions were led by Energy (+11.8%) while Materials fell 9.1%, so the aggregate gain did not spread broadly. Goldman's September flash PMIs show input-price pressures accelerating faster than output prices, adding margin risk on top of the earnings divide. Separately, the US 10-year real yield rose from 2.44% to 2.76% between 1 and 23 September as breadth deteriorated, raising the rerating hurdle for a broad set of equities beyond the current earnings winners. The piece frames the trade as conditional. If post-report Q4 estimate upgrades spread to most sectors while RSP/SPY stays depressed, the equal-weight catch-up case strengthens. If cuts stay widespread and RSP/SPY keeps weakening, the index stays propped by a narrow group of earnings winners. The first post-report Q4 revisions are called the decision point.
